lesson.title: Skydiver Graphs and BASE Jump Speed Run
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 1 Lesson 5: Skydiver Graphs and BASE Jump Speed Run

assessmentSettings.feedbackPolicy: Use native Buzz feedback for Questions 1-5. Use this metadata and the Essay a. line for BusyBee grading on Questions 6-7.

gradingDesign.part1: Questions 1-5 are fixed graph questions because every student sees the same scripted jump.
gradingDesign.part2: Questions 6-7 are student-dependent because body position, deploy time, deploy altitude, final time, landing speed, and graph evidence depend on the student's speed-run attempt.
gradingDesign.studentDependentRule: Do not grade challenge values as fixed numeric answers. Compare the written strategy to the uploaded/copied challenge evidence.

requiredUploads: BASE Jump Speed Run evidence image or screenshot
successCriteria: Landing speed is 8 m/s or less

humanReviewTriggers: Student response conflicts with the uploaded challenge evidence.
Evidence upload is missing, unreadable, or does not show the result and graphs.
Student claims success but the evidence shows no parachute or landing speed above 8 m/s.
Student gives a plausible strategy explanation that does not fit the rubric cleanly.
Student describes graph features incorrectly but the evidence suggests partial understanding.

questions.objective: Read increasing velocity from a velocity-time graph.
questions.answerKey: The skydiver speeds up from rest to terminal velocity.
questions.feedbackFocus: A rising velocity-time graph means speed is increasing.

questions.objective: Identify when terminal velocity begins on the scripted graph.
questions.feedbackFocus: Terminal velocity begins where the velocity-time graph first becomes horizontal.

questions.objective: Connect a horizontal velocity-time graph to constant velocity.
questions.answerKey: The skydiver is moving at constant terminal velocity.
questions.feedbackFocus: A horizontal velocity-time graph means the velocity is not changing.

questions.objective: Estimate acceleration from the slope of a velocity-time graph.
questions.feedbackFocus: Use slope = change in velocity divided by change in time.

questions.objective: Interpret negative acceleration after parachute deployment.
questions.answerKey: The parachute decreases the skydiver's downward velocity.
questions.feedbackFocus: Negative acceleration means the downward velocity is decreasing.

questions.objective: Submit challenge evidence for a student-dependent run.
questions.prompt: Upload your BASE Jump Speed Run evidence image.
questions.requiredEvidence: Evidence should show the challenge result, final time, landing speed, deploy time, deploy altitude, velocity-time graph, and acceleration-time graph.

criteria: Evidence shows the challenge result and key landing values.
Evidence includes both velocity-time and acceleration-time graphs.
Upload is present but one required value or graph is missing.
Evidence is partially cut off but the run can still be interpreted.
Evidence shows a real attempt even if the challenge was not successful.
Evidence does not show the challenge attempt.

feedback.partialCredit: Upload a clearer evidence image that shows the result, landing values, and both graphs.
feedback.noCredit: Return to the challenge, complete a run, and download or screenshot the challenge evidence.

questions.objective: Explain a challenge strategy using body position, parachute timing, and graph evidence.
questions.prompt: Explain your speed-run strategy. How did body position and parachute timing affect your final time and landing speed, and what graph evidence supports your explanation?
questions.requiredEvidence: Student should refer to their own final time, landing speed, deploy timing, deploy altitude, body position, velocity-time graph, or acceleration-time graph.

criteria: Explains how at least one body position changed falling speed.
Explains how parachute timing affected final time and landing speed.
Uses graph evidence such as rising velocity, terminal velocity, or negative acceleration after deployment.
Describes a strategy but gives limited graph evidence.
Uses graph evidence but does not clearly connect it to body position, parachute timing, or safe landing speed.
Explains a failed attempt with a reasonable correction.
Does not refer to the student's challenge evidence.

commonMisconceptions: A negative acceleration-time value means the skydiver is moving upward.
Deploying the parachute always guarantees a safe landing.
A horizontal velocity-time graph means the skydiver stopped.

feedback.partialCredit: Add one specific graph detail from your evidence and connect it to your body position or deploy timing.
feedback.noCredit: Use your challenge evidence: name your body position, deploy timing, final time, landing result, and one graph feature.
